name: qwen-vllm-serve
description: Serve a Qwen-family chat model on vLLM (OpenAI-compatible, port 8000, tool calling enabled) on a single 48GB-class GPU. The model is yours to declare: replace the SET-ME placeholder in service.start with the Hugging Face repo id you intend to serve — verified with community AWQ-INT4 builds of Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3.8-27B (Apache 2.0). Tool-call parser: the default 'hermes' fits Qwen3.5/3.6 lineage; switch the extra_args value to 'qwen3_coder' for Qwen3.8 / Qwen3-Coder lineage, which emits the XML function-call format. The install step is CUDA-driver-aware: PyPI's default vllm/torch wheels are CUDA-13 builds, and on hosts whose driver reports CUDA 12.x (e.g. driver 570) they fail at engine start with 'driver too old' — on such hosts the script force-reinstalls the +cu129 torch family and the +cu129 vllm wheel from the vLLM GitHub release, which run on any 12.x driver via CUDA minor-version compatibility. First start downloads the model via vLLM itself (~16 GB for a 27B AWQ build), hence the generous service.ready deadline.

phases.script:
set -e
cuda_major=$(nvidia-smi | grep -oE 'CUDA Version: [0-9]+' | grep -oE '[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo 0)
pip install 'vllm==0.28.0'
if [ "$cuda_major" = "12" ]; then
  pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps 'torch==2.13.0+cu129' 'torchvision==0.28.0+cu129' 'torchaudio==2.11.0+cu129' torchcodec --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu129
  pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps 'https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/releases/download/v0.28.0/vllm-0.28.0+cu129-cp38-abi3-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl'
fi
python3 -c 'import torch, vllm; torch.zeros(1).cuda(); print("stack-ok", torch.__version__, vllm.__version__)'
